topic: Topic Empirical AI/ML research. Pick one open, concrete question about the behavior of machine-learning models — for example: training dynamics and generalization (grokking, double descent), in-context learning in small transformers, calibration of model confidence, prompt/format sensitivity of language models, tokenization effects, or optimizer behavior — that can be investigated rigorously with small-scale experiments runnable on a single machine (CPU or Apple-Silicon MPS), and study it end-to-end.

hypotheses.statement: For modular addition mod 31 with a width-128 two-layer ReLU MLP, cross-entropy loss, a fixed 50% training split, and four matched seeds, a no-decay fork started at the first checkpoint with at least 99% training accuracy and given an adaptive output temperature that matches the centered-logit RMS of its paired AdamW fork every 50 steps will reach sustained 95% test accuracy within 20% of the AdamW fork's post-checkpoint step count in at least three of four seeds.
hypotheses.rationale: This is a direct causal test of the survey's central gap: whether AdamW accelerates cross-entropy grokking mainly through effective logit scale. Matching logit scale without changing the parameter update rule isolates the proposed mediator more sharply than correlating norm, logits, and grokking time in independent runs.

hypotheses.statement: Under the same mod-31 MLP protocol but with one-hot MSE, an adaptive output-temperature fork that matches the output RMS of a paired AdamW run will differ from that AdamW run's median post-memorization grokking delay by at least 40%, whereas a no-decay fork projected every 50 steps onto the AdamW run's parameter norm will differ by no more than 25%.
hypotheses.rationale: The survey reports that MSE pins output scale and may leave parameter norm acting through another route, but this loss-dependent contrast has not been established in the interpretable two-layer MLP setting. The result would distinguish true norm dependence from a cross-entropy-specific logit-scale mechanism.

hypotheses.statement: At a memorized cross-entropy checkpoint, adding a rank-one class-common component to the output matrix that doubles total squared parameter norm while leaving every softmax probability unchanged, then decaying only that component until total norm crosses the threshold fitted from ordinary AdamW runs, will change the sustained-95%-test-accuracy grokking step by less than 10% relative to an unmodified no-decay fork across four matched seeds.
hypotheses.rationale: A class-common logit component is exactly invisible to softmax probabilities, so it can manipulate raw parameter norm without changing predictions or centered logit scale. If crossing a total-norm threshold were itself causal, this intervention should alter grokking; if logit scale is the operative variable, it should not. This directly probes the survey's tension between norm-threshold and logit-mediation accounts.

hypotheses.statement: In cross-entropy mod-31 MLP runs forked immediately after memorization, weight decay applied only to the centered output-layer weights, with its coefficient calibrated by a 200-step deterministic pilot to match the initial total-norm shrinkage of full-model AdamW, will produce a median grokking delay within 25% of full-model AdamW; matched-shrinkage decay applied only to the first layer will have a median delay at least 1.5 times that of full-model AdamW.
hypotheses.rationale: If weight decay works mainly by reducing effective logit scale, decay acting directly on the probability-relevant output map should reproduce most of the benefit even when hidden-layer norm is not regularized. This layer-localized intervention separates logit control from generic norm reduction and representation simplification.

hypotheses.statement: For memorized cross-entropy ReLU MLP checkpoints, the function-preserving transformations W1 and b1 multiplied by c and W2 divided by c, using c in {0.5, 2}, will change total squared parameter norm by at least a factor of two but leave the subsequent median grokking step under SGD without momentum within 15% of the c=1 fork; consequently, an absolute total-norm first-passage predictor fitted on c=1 runs will have at least 50% median relative timing error on the rescaled forks.
hypotheses.rationale: Positive homogeneity permits large changes in parameter norm without changing logits at the intervention point. Using plain SGD avoids Adam's coordinatewise state as an immediate confound. This tests whether the norm threshold described in the survey is architecture-parameterization dependent rather than a function-level causal quantity.

hypotheses.statement: With cross-entropy on mod-31 addition, AdamW enabled only after the first checkpoint with at least 99% training accuracy will reach sustained 95% test accuracy within 20% of the total step count of continuously applied AdamW, while AdamW disabled at that checkpoint after being applied only during memorization will reduce the post-memorization grokking delay by no more than 20% relative to a never-decayed control in at least three of four matched seeds.
hypotheses.rationale: The survey does not establish when weight decay exerts its decisive effect. A post-memorization-only benefit would localize the mechanism to the delayed-generalization phase and support checkpoint-fork interventions, whereas a strong pre-memorization carryover would implicate early representation or optimizer-state formation.

hypotheses.statement: In cross-entropy checkpoint forks where output temperature alone accelerates grokking by at least 30%, the centered-logit RMS will complete half of its total pre-grokking change at least 20% of the post-memorization interval before the hidden-activation Fourier Coefficient Ratio completes half of its change, while the Fourier midpoint will occur within 10% of the sustained-95%-test-accuracy step in at least three of four seeds.
hypotheses.rationale: This tests a staged mechanism connecting the survey's logit-scale and representation-level accounts: logit-scale correction should precede, rather than merely accompany, the emergence of Fourier structure, while Fourier organization should remain tightly coupled to actual generalization. Either temporal ordering would clarify which measurement is mediator versus marker.

hypotheses.statement: A first-passage predictor fitted only on four AdamW coefficients and four seeds of mod-31 MLP training will, on held-out temperature-only, softmax-null-component-decay, and function-preserving-rescaling interventions, achieve median relative grokking-time error below 25% when its crossing variable is centered-logit RMS under cross-entropy but above 50% when its crossing variable is total squared parameter norm; under MSE, the logit-RMS predictor will not outperform the norm predictor by more than five percentage points.
hypotheses.rationale: Prior norm-threshold and logit-mediation results are mostly assessed within intervention families where norm and logits covary. Testing both predictors on interventions designed to dissociate them evaluates out-of-distribution causal generalization and directly addresses whether the preferred predictor changes with the loss.

design.summary: Use four seeded modular-addition grokking runs to test whether forcing total parameter norm through an AdamW-fitted threshold via a softmax-invisible rank-one output component changes the sustained-95%-test-accuracy step.
design.protocol:
1. Start in a newly created empty workspace. Set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=off, MPLCONFIGDIR=<workspace>/.mplconfig, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1. Create the environment with `python -m venv --system-site-packages .venv`. First try importing torch, numpy, and matplotlib from system packages; install only missing packages with `python -m pip install --no-cache-dir <package>`. Use CPU only, float64 tensors, one Torch thread, `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, and disable MPS/CUDA. Delete pip, matplotlib, Python bytecode, and build caches before training.
2. Implement `workspace_bytes()` by recursively summing allocated file sizes (`st_blocks*512` when available, otherwise `st_size`) within the workspace. Record the largest observed value as `maximum_workspace_bytes`. Run this guard before dependency installation, after installation, every 100 optimization steps, and before and after writing outputs. Delete caches immediately if usage exceeds 1,500,000,000 bytes; terminate with a compact flat results.json carrying `audit_disk_valid=false` if it remains above 1,800,000,000 bytes. Never write model checkpoints. Keep model and optimizer snapshots only in RAM, and save only results.json, curves.npz, and result.png.
3. For each matched seed s in {0,1,2,3}, generate the complete modular-addition dataset over p=23: inputs are all 529 ordered pairs (a,b) in {0,...,22}^2 and the class is y=(a+b) mod 23. Construct a class-stratified split using NumPy `Generator(1000+s)`: independently permute the 23 examples of each target class and put the first 9 in training. Thus every seed has exactly 207 training and 322 test examples, with 9 training examples per class. Use full-batch training and preserve this fixed ordering throughout a run.
4. Use this model exactly: separate learned embedding tables E_a and E_b of shape 23x32; concatenate E_a[a] and E_b[b] into 64 dimensions; apply an affine layer 64x128 with bias, ReLU, then an affine output layer W of shape 23x128 with bias. Initialize all matrix entries from N(0,1/sqrt(fan_in)) and all biases to zero using `torch.manual_seed(2000+s)`. Define total squared parameter norm as the sum of squares of every embedding, weight, and bias parameter. For all losses and predictions use centered logits `z - mean(z,dim=1,keepdim=True)`, which is exactly softmax-equivalent to the raw logits.
5. Define an evaluation point every 10 optimizer steps, including step 0. At each evaluation compute full training cross-entropy, training accuracy, test accuracy, and total norm. Define memorization as the first evaluation beginning a run of 10 consecutive evaluation points with training accuracy 1.0 and training cross-entropy <=0.02. Define the sustained-95% grokking step G as the first evaluation beginning a run of 20 consecutive evaluation points with test accuracy >=0.95; report the first point of that run, not its confirmation point. Resolve this online by retaining the preceding 19 values. A run that lacks such a window by its maximum step is censored.
6. Run one ordinary AdamW reference trajectory for each seed from initialization, with learning rate 0.001, betas (0.9,0.98), epsilon 1e-8, weight_decay 0.1, and no learning-rate schedule, for at most 25,000 steps. Record compact scalar curves every 10 steps. Stop a reference run after confirming its sustained grokking window or at 25,000 steps. For each uncensored reference run record G_ref_s and the total parameter norm N_ref_s at G_ref_s. Fit the single ordinary-run norm threshold T as the median of the four N_ref_s values. All four reference runs must grok; otherwise set `audit_reference_valid=false` and do not claim support.
7. From each reference scalar curve choose the latest evaluation step C_s satisfying all of: it is at or after that seed's memorization step; it is at least 200 steps before G_ref_s; its instantaneous test accuracy is below 0.95; and its norm N_s brackets T after the intervention, meaning N_s < T < sqrt(2)*N_s. Replay that seed deterministically from initialization to C_s and retain the model and AdamW optimizer state in RAM. Verify replayed loss, accuracy, and norm agree with the recorded values within 1e-10. If no such C_s exists, set that seed's `audit_checkpoint_valid_s=false`; such a run is not eligible to support the hypothesis.
8. At checkpoint C_s, make two bitwise copies of the model and optimizer state. Set optimizer weight_decay to 0 in both copies while retaining all Adam moments and the same learning rate. The first copy is the unmodified no-decay baseline. The second is the intervention fork. Only the intervention receives the frozen class-common output component described next; all ordinary trainable parameters continue to receive identical no-decay Adam updates in both forks.
9. Let mu be the mean of the 23 rows of the checkpoint output matrix W. Construct a deterministic unit vector q orthogonal to mu: choose the standard basis vector e_k whose orthogonal residual `e_k - mu*(mu dot e_k)/(mu dot mu)` has the largest norm, normalize that residual, and use e_0 if mu is exactly zero. Let S_s be the checkpoint's total squared parameter norm and set `a0=q*sqrt(S_s/23)`. The intervention's conceptual output matrix is `W_int=W+1_23*a^T`, initially with a=a0. Since mu dot a0=0, its total squared parameter norm is exactly 2*S_s apart from floating-point error. The intervention raw logits are `W h + b + (a dot h)*1_23`; the loss and prediction code must analytically remove the common scalar and use the same centered task logits as the baseline, so the common component receives no gradient and cannot affect Adam state.
10. Before the first fork update, evaluate all 529 examples and record: maximum absolute difference between baseline and intervention softmax probabilities; maximum absolute centered-logit difference; maximum absolute cross-entropy difference; number of prediction mismatches; class-common residual error `max |(z_int-z_base)-mean_class(z_int-z_base)|`; relative error of the intended squared-norm ratio, `abs(S_int/S_base-2)`; and mu dot a0. Require respective bounds of 1e-10, 1e-10, 1e-12, zero, 1e-10, 1e-10, and 1e-10. These are the initial exact-null audit checks.
11. Continue both forks in lockstep for at most 8,000 post-checkpoint steps. Feed identical full batches and execute baseline then intervention updates in a fixed order. In the intervention only, propose a linear decay `a=a0*max(0,1-j/200)` at post-fork step j. Define X_s as the first absolute optimization step C_s+j at which the intervention's conceptual total norm, computed using W+1_23*a^T and all other current parameters, is <=T. Once X_s occurs, stop decaying a and hold its current value fixed for the remainder of the run. If no crossing has occurred by j=200, set a=0 and check once more; if the norm is still above T, set `audit_crossing_valid_s=false`. This schedule changes only the frozen class-common component.
12. At every 10-step evaluation, compute baseline and intervention train/test metrics, conceptual total norms, and the exact-null audit quantities over all 529 examples. Also record the maximum absolute difference between corresponding ordinary trainable parameters and Adam first- and second-moment tensors in the two forks. Require throughout the run: probability error <=1e-10, centered-logit error <=1e-10, cross-entropy error <=1e-12, zero prediction mismatches, class-common residual <=1e-10, and maximum model/optimizer-state drift <=1e-12. Set `audit_invariance_valid_s` from these conditions.
13. Continue until both forks have confirmed their 20-evaluation sustained-95% windows, then run 20 additional evaluations to detect immediate loss of the criterion; otherwise stop at 8,000 post-checkpoint steps. Record absolute grokking steps G_base_s and G_intervention_s. Define `R_s=abs(G_intervention_s-G_base_s)/G_base_s`. If exactly one fork is censored, set R_s=1.0. If both are censored, set R_s=null and `audit_grokking_valid_s=false`. Define R_max=max(R_0,R_1,R_2,R_3) only when all four R_s values are non-null.
14. The hypothesis is supported if and only if all four reference, replay, checkpoint, initial-invariance, crossing, ongoing-invariance, grokking, and disk audit flags are true and R_max<0.10. It is refuted if all validity flags are true and R_max>=0.10. Invalid audits or two-sided censoring produce the prespecified outcome `inconclusive_invalid`, never support. Also report whether each baseline/intervention grokking step occurred before, at, or after X_s; this is descriptive and does not replace the R_max decision rule.
15. Write a flat results.json with scalar keys only, including at minimum: `status`, `hypothesis_supported`, `T`, `seed_0_X` through `seed_3_X`, `seed_0_baseline_grokking_step` through `seed_3_baseline_grokking_step`, corresponding intervention steps and R values, `R_max`, per-seed checkpoint and reference steps, per-seed initial and run-maximum probability/centered-logit/cross-entropy/common-residual errors, norm-ratio errors, prediction mismatches, model-state drift, optimizer-state drift, every per-seed audit-validity flag, aggregate audit flags, and `maximum_workspace_bytes`. Use JSON null for censored or undefined numeric values; do not use NaN.
16. Save compressed scalar curves as curves.npz. Produce result.png at 160 dpi with two columns and four seed-colored curves: the left panel plots baseline and intervention test accuracy against absolute step, with horizontal 0.95 and vertical X_s markers; the right panel plots baseline and intervention conceptual total norm with horizontal line T and vertical X_s markers. Use solid lines for baseline and dashed lines for intervention. Close the matplotlib figure, delete .mplconfig and all remaining caches, update `maximum_workspace_bytes`, rewrite results.json if that maximum changed, and verify that results.json, curves.npz, and result.png all exist and the workspace remains below 1,800,000,000 bytes.
metrics: T: median total parameter norm at the sustained-95% grokking step in the four ordinary AdamW reference runs
X_s: first absolute step at which seed s's intervention conceptual total norm is less than or equal to T
G_base_s and G_intervention_s: first evaluation steps beginning 20 consecutive 10-step evaluations with test accuracy at least 0.95
R_s: abs(G_intervention_s-G_base_s)/G_base_s, with R_max equal to the maximum over four matched seeds
Initial squared-norm ratio error: abs(S_intervention/S_baseline-2) immediately after adding the rank-one component
Invariance errors: run-wide maxima of probability, centered-logit, cross-entropy, and class-common-residual differences over all 529 examples, plus prediction mismatch count
Trajectory audit: maximum absolute difference between corresponding trainable parameters and Adam moment tensors in the matched forks
Validity metrics: per-seed reference-grokking, checkpoint-bracketing, threshold-crossing, replay, invariance, grokking, and disk-quota flags
Maximum workspace bytes: largest recursively measured workspace allocation during setup, training, and output generation
design.expected_if_true: All audits pass, each intervention starts with squared norm ratio 2 within 1e-10, each X_s exists, probability and centered-logit errors remain at or below 1e-10 with zero prediction mismatches, all forks grok, and every R_s is below 0.10 so R_max<0.10; in the expected exact-null case the paired grokking steps and R_s values will be identical and zero.
design.expected_if_false: With all validity audits passing and all four comparisons defined, at least one intervention changes the sustained-95% grokking step by 10% or more, giving R_max>=0.10; a norm-threshold-causal pattern would additionally show intervention grokking delayed toward or beyond X_s despite unchanged probabilities before the crossing.

iterations.notes:
The experiment never reached the intervention test: all four calibration runs completed 15,000 steps but had grokking_step = -1, so no valid norm thresholds or matched intervention forks were produced. Although every seed memorized the training set (train accuracy 1.0 and cross-entropy between 4.31e-06 and 0.00127), best test accuracy was only 0.126-0.208, far below the sustained 95% criterion. Therefore the reported protocol-level "refuted" decision does not constitute evidence that the invisible norm manipulation changes grokking time.

Revision instructions: First validate a grokking-producing baseline by extending the training horizon and tuning the established grokking controls—dataset/train split, model size, learning rate, AdamW weight decay, and modular-task setup—until ordinary runs reliably reach sustained 95% test accuracy across the intended seeds. Then fit thresholds only from successful ordinary runs, create matched no-decay and intervention forks from audited memorized checkpoints, verify probability and centered-logit invariance numerically, require the manipulated total norm to cross the fitted threshold, and compare paired sustained-grokking steps.

The experiment produced no results.json and was killed after exceeding the 2048 MB workspace quota. Consequently, there are no reported values for the four seeds, threshold crossings, audit checks, grokking steps, or R_max, so the hypothesis was not actually evaluated.

Revision instructions: Reduce disk usage by disabling large checkpoints and verbose traces, retaining only the memorized checkpoint and compact per-step metrics, and deleting temporary artifacts between seeds. Write results.json incrementally and atomically after each seed so partial diagnostics survive termination, monitor workspace usage during execution, and rerun all four matched seeds with the required probability, centered-logit, threshold-crossing, and sustained-95%-accuracy audits.

The experiment was killed after 10.6 seconds because the workspace exceeded the 2048 MB disk quota, and the process also received a wall-clock timeout signal. No results.json was produced, so there are no exact-null audit values, threshold crossings, per-seed R_s values, or R_max with which to test the hypothesis.

Revision instructions: Re-run in a clean workspace and keep total workspace usage below the quota: create the venv with system site packages if available, install only minimal CPU dependencies without pip caches, and delete caches/build artifacts and unnecessary checkpoints. Add an early disk-usage guard, save only compact scalar/curve data and the required PNG, then ensure the run completes all four matched seeds and writes a flat results.json containing invariance errors, T, each X_s, baseline/intervention grokking steps, each R_s, R_max, audit-validity flags, and maximum workspace bytes.

The experiment was killed after exceeding the 2048 MB workspace quota, and results.json was not produced. Therefore, none of the required headline metrics—four matched-seed grokking steps, R_s values, R_max, norm-ratio errors, invariance errors, or validity audits—are available, so the hypothesis was not tested.

Revision instructions: Reduce disk usage before rerunning: use a lightweight venv with only essential dependencies, avoid caching packages or checkpoints, set PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1, delete pip caches/build artifacts, and store only the memorized checkpoint plus compact scalar trajectories rather than per-step model states. Add an early recursive workspace-size guard well below 2048 MB, ensure failures immediately write a flat results.json with an error field, then execute the complete four-seed protocol and verify all audits and headline metrics are present.
